Rationale: new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') is UTC midnight, so extended end dates read one day short west of UTC
Rationale: a Stripe pre-auth dies after ~5-7 days and no webhook watches rentals.deposit_hold_payment_intent_id (GMT, Aug 2026)
Rationale: 3 days is the last point an operator can refresh a hold before a weekend swallows it
Rationale: liveHold:false is not 'resolved' — it also means still authorising or another worker owns the row
Rationale: released/skipped/lost_race/chain_expired are correct outcomes; shouting 'failed' at them trains operators to ignore real failures
Rationale: a single-rental dispatch inherits the cron's due-filters, so zero results must read as 'nothing needed doing'
Rationale: hold row actions split by consequence not frequency; gates stay per-branch and an all-gated menu renders no trigger
Rationale: every hold-menu handler stops propagation because the table row itself navigates
Rationale: supabase.functions.invoke resolves {data,error} on non-2xx, so a 500 would otherwise show a success toast
Rationale: the refresh engine cancels the live authorisation before placing its replacement, so it sits behind a confirm and isAdmin()
Rationale: refresh-deposit-holds accepts the cron secret or a super-admin JWT, so a tenant head_admin is legitimately refused
Rationale: match the refresh outcome by rentalId, not position, so a widened batch cannot report someone else's result
Rationale: verification sync must be tenant-scoped and must never overwrite manually_verified; a uuid compared to '' fails silently
Rationale: Security Deposit is excluded from outstanding amounts — it is a Stripe pre-auth hold, not money owed
Rationale: a fresh PAYG rental has no accruals, so outstandingBalance is 0 and Record Payment wrongly said 'no outstanding balance'
Rationale: status 'Credit' is an unallocated prepayment and counts as received; 'Pending' is an unpaid checkout and must not
Rationale: a global find for Extension Insurance made older extensions inherit a newer extension's unpaid remainder
Rationale: the extension_id must be stamped or apply-payment's FIFO allocator drains the oldest extension instead
Rationale: Supabase Storage rejects keys containing characters such as macOS's U+202F, so filenames are sanitised
Rationale: extras day-count must match the algorithm used at rental creation or a DST crossing drifts from what was charged
Rationale: `{canEdit && …}` tested the function object, so the date/location Edit gates never fired and viewers could edit
Rationale: the no-hold Add Hold branch was the one ungated placement path, and add-hold-dialog carries no check of its own
Rationale: when the hold CHECK constraint went from 7 to 11 values the new statuses fell through to a 'No hold placed' lie
Rationale: processing/refreshing keep the outgoing hold's expiry date, so rendering it would shout 'lapsed' over a healthy replacement
Rationale: no placement button while an authorisation is in flight — a second hold would double-hold the customer's card
Rationale: 'capturing' offers no verify because a PI at requires_capture maps back to 'held', stamping over a capture in flight
Rationale: deduct-from-deposit captures the disputed PaymentIntent, so a chargeback blocks the button entirely
Rationale: Bonzah cover must start tomorrow Pacific, so a trip ending today has zero insurable days
Rationale: selling a new Bonzah policy requires live mode (test mode issues sandbox cover); viewing existing policies is left alone
Rationale: the ID-waiver banner is permanent because a later claim, dispute or insurance query must see it without audit-log digging
Rationale: the software-feedback prompt only follows a review opened by CLOSING a rental — after a manual edit it would be ambush
Rationale: with an installment plan the upfront lands entirely on the Rental charge, leaving fee ledger rows un-decremented but settled
Rationale: paying by Stripe auto-places the deposit hold because the card was just collected; a manual record does not
Rationale: if the webhook has not allocated within ~6s, apply-payment is called as fallback; a unique ledger index blocks double-processing
Rationale: the duplicate PAYG Add Payment footer was removed to keep the operator anchored on the PAYG section
Rationale: payg_closed_at is a leftover flag on migrated auto-extension rentals and must not be read as 'closed'
Rationale: the timezone footer exists because operators could not tell which zone the dates were in after the off-by-one bug
Rationale: deposit hold columns live on rentals, not payments, which is exactly why an expiring authorisation goes unnoticed
